fields.claim_quote:
If an input vertex $p$
lies inside the diametral circle on line segment $ab$,
the perpendicular projection of $p$ on the line joining
$a$ and $b$ lies on the line segment joining $a$ and $b$.
Let the point of projection be $m$.  Further,
$\angle apb < \pi/2$.
fields.explanation: The original unscaled points a=(−1,0),b=(1,0),p=(0,1/2) are preserved. Mathlib EuclideanSpace gives norm(p)=1/2 and ray inner product−3/4; the actual EuclideanGeometry.angle is not acute. The old certificate had only named an integer dot-product test acuteAt.
fields.flaw: If an input vertex p lies inside the diametral circle on segment ab, then angle apb is less than π/2.

0043 | Let us first consider the 2D problem (see
0044 | Fig.~\ref{fig:aux2d}).  If an input vertex $p$
0045 | lies inside the diametral circle on line segment $ab$,
0046 | the perpendicular projection of $p$ on the line joining
0047 | $a$ and $b$ lies on the line segment joining $a$ and $b$.
0048 | Let the point of projection be $m$.  Further,
0049 | $\angle apb < \pi/2$.  If the point $m$ is added to the
0050 | PLC, $p$ does not lie inside the diametral circle of
0051 | edge $am$ or $mb$, but $m$ may not be the most optimal
0052 | location of an auxiliary Steiner point because it may be
0053 | arbitrarily close to $a$ or $b$.  Thus, we perturb the
0054 | vertex $m$ to a location $m^{'}$ such that $p$ does not
0055 | lie inside the new diametral circles, \emph{and} its
0056 | location maximizes the minimum distance from all other
0057 | vertices.
fields.witness: Take a=(-1,0), b=(1,0), and p=(0,1/2). The diametral circle has center (0,0) and radius 1, and ‖p‖²=1/4<1, so p is strictly inside. Its perpendicular projection m=(0,0) lies on segment ab.
